chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is your livelihood?' I said, 'I have two slaves and two camels.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Conceal that from your brethren, for if they do not harm you, they will not benefit you either.'
ai.seo_question: Why should one conceal their wealth from relatives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises concealing one's assets from kin to avoid the 'curse of the good' (lazim al-khayr), where relatives expect perpetual support without reciprocation. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on financial prudence and the psychological burden of obligatory charity (sadaqat al-awlah) within the extended family structure.
